# Acerola — Local-First Comic & Manga Reader

> Official summary file for LLMs, AI agents, and search engine assistants. Provides structured context about the Acerola project: what it is, how its platforms fit together, and where to find its documentation and source code.

## About Acerola
Acerola is a comic and manga reader that syncs your local library directly between your own devices over P2P — no cloud, no account, no server to trust. It's a monorepo: each platform lives on its own, with its own stack, and none depends directly on another. All of them consume the shared P2P libraries via a local path dependency.

- **Documentation**: https://docs.acerola-comic.com
- **GitHub**: https://github.com/Vinicius-Gabriel-P-Leitao/acerola-reader
- **License**: MPL-2.0

---

## Platforms

### Android
Native app in Kotlin + Jetpack Compose.

### Desktop
App in Rust + Tauri + Svelte 5.

### Relay
Remote access service with no port forwarding, deployable to a VPS.

### lib/p2p
Shared P2P library in Rust, built on iroh/QUIC.

### lib/relay
Vendored iroh relay code, the base for the relay service.

---

## How the pieces connect
`acerola/android` and `acerola/desktop` never see each other directly — each implements its own FFI/binding to consume `lib/p2p`. All device-to-device communication is either direct P2P (LAN via mDNS) or through the relay when devices aren't on the same network.
